findings.asked: Complete the square, then state the minimum value and where it occurs.
findings.wentWrong: More candidates than expected were unfamiliar with the method; some could not interpret the minimum and its x-value; some differentiated instead.
findings.rule: (x + a) squared + b: minimum b at x = -a.

findings.asked: Complete the square; hence find the minimum point.
findings.wentWrong: Many used differentiation and lost both marks; those who used the form often substituted x = 4 back into the original to get y = 8 instead of reading it off.
findings.rule: 'Hence' means use the completed square - the constant is the minimum.

findings.wentWrong: Adding 49 instead of subtracting; 7 written where -7 was the x-value.
findings.rule: (x + 7) squared means the turning point is at x = -7; subtract the added square.

findings.asked: Complete the square; hence find the minimum.
findings.wentWrong: The constant term went wrong from a half-coefficient slip; in (ii) 'hence' was ignored and calculus used, scoring zero even when the arithmetic was right.
findings.rule: Read 'hence' as an instruction about method.

ruleToRemember: (x + a) squared - a squared + c; the minimum value is the constant, at x = -a; when a question says 'hence', use that form - differentiation earns nothing there.
